why: What a plugin may use, each with a version raised only when it changes in a way that breaks its users. A plugin.json lists what it uses in "uses": {"<name>": <version>}; one this engine does not offer at that version is not turned on (blocked). "also": older versions still offered. "transitional": still works, but release.py check-plugin reminds that it goes away (the words say what replaces it). "paths" and "modules": the files under the engine a plugin may run, read or import for it; "functions": the public ones of a module, "others": what check-plugin says about the rest.

dc.post.what: altention dc post (--file, --wait, --board, --activity, --create; @audit, @notify), and with --file x.png the file x.png.source.json beside it, what the picture was drawn from (altention/sources.py: kind, lang, tool, source). A change to that file's format raises this version.

activity.pages.what: plugin.json "activity": {"pages"} and what the bot writes for a page opened

py.config.what: altention.config: root, instance_dir, settings, setting, machines, this_machine, engine_on, ssh_aliases
